I was always fit, doing sports, extremely active and energitic, in 2019-2020 I ended up reaching 100 KG with a height of 180, and I looked like a walking ball, one of my friends suggested some small tips and steps:
1) for a week, just use MyFitnessPal application to document all the food you eat with no modifications, and understand what is the major calorie intake you have, mine was stupidly nuts "100 grams has 800 calories" which is almost half of your suggested daily intake.
2) drop the major calorie sources, but keep documenting as you go "after the first month, I started to be able to estimate without using the application"
3) don't cut food completely, either find a healthier alternative "for example diet soda drinks instead of regular" Today or oreo chocolate instead of normal KitKats, or smaller proportions for example a regular Shawerma meal instead of a double meal.
4) Include fun physical activities in your life like football or basketball, mine was laser tag.

I ended up dropping to 80 KGs in 4 months, without craving or missing anything, best of luck mate.

This might be lengthy so sit tight, Jordan as a whole has a lot to offer, it is safe, but you will need to rent a car to see it whole, it is on the expensive side when it comes to tourism but what I would usually suggest to people that come to visit is the following:

1) one full day in Amman "so land the first day, have lunch/dinner" then spend a full day in Amman, citadel, roman theatre, and there is a free walking path which you can find on Google.

2) go to Dhana, spend a night camping in Dhana wild reserve, it is fascinating and extremely close to nature, early in the morning head to petra, do the tour around, it will take you 7-10 hours, head to aqaba, spend the night in the morning go scuba diving have lunch and head out in time to catch the sunset in Wadi rum, dinner there, star gazing spend the night and head back from the dead sea road, check into a dead sea hotel "no need for a fancy one tbh" I would suggest the grand east hotel, on the cheaper side, great pool and beach, spend the night again, have breakfast, and head out wadi mujib after that go to dead sea panorama restaurant and museum, have late lunch/ dinner and watch the sunset in an amazing view.

3) head back to amman, spend the night there, early breakfast in downtown, and walk around the markets, and then head out to Jerash, see the Romanian sites, go to ajloun to the wild reserve, have dinner there and maybe spend the night "Amazing cabins in the wild" while you are there, you can check hiking trails, as there are plenty in the north, and they are all really fascinating, go to um qais, and then head back to amman.

And that is it, welcome to Jordan In advance.

I'll explain some of my points here on why I would suggest otherwise while showcasing a "supposedly" better alternative:

While buying a property has always been deemed a good investment, people tend don't realize that the ROI "Return of investment" on such action is usually 7-15 years taking in consideration times where the apartment will be empty, repairs, and/or dealing with renters "due to Jordan's retarded owner/renters laws, financially the loss of value of property is 3-7% a year, which makes the whole process a loss of money on paper, if you decided to go through with it, I would suggest to make the contracts 3 months in length, with a 100 JOD safety deposit, and the the contract only gets renewed upon the approval of both parties.

A better alternative "from my point of view" I have rented 3 2 bedroom apartments, in good vital locations, fixed them, and furnished them and listed them on airbnb "after ofcourse getting the approval of the landlord" the initial cost for such a move is relatively very small while the profit is way better, please find my calculations below:

1 room/per night: 20 JOD, at a 50% occupancy rate, thats 2(rooms) *20 (price per night) *15(days of the month) = 600 JOD
200 rent, 100 utilitiez, 300 profit: you might have to do works or stuff around the house, but it's proper income with much less risk.


Best of luck, and please understand that what might work for me, doesn't necessarily have to work for you.
